props.label: Services
props.html:
Our services

Everything your outdoor space needs, under one licence

Landscape design

Concept plans, planting schemes and clear drawings you can build from, including council-ready plans where a project needs them.

Paving

Patios, paths and driveways laid on properly prepared bases so they don't lift, dip or crack when the clay moves.

Retaining walls

Engineered walls with real drainage behind them. On a sloping Macarthur block, that's what keeps soil and structures where they belong.

Turf laying

Fresh lawn on a graded, conditioned base, with the right turf variety for our heat and frost swings so it takes and stays green.

Gardening & planting

Garden beds, hedges and planting chosen for local conditions, plus tidy-ups that bring a tired yard back to life.

Mulching

Quality mulch that locks in moisture through a dry western Sydney summer and keeps weeds down between seasons.

Tree removal

Safe removal of unwanted or risky trees, with the mess cleared out. Handy on bush-fringe blocks that need space around the home.

Weeding

Beds and paths cleared and kept clear, so all the good work doesn't disappear under weeds a month later.

What changes your price

A few things move a landscaping quote up or down. We walk through all of them on site so there are no surprises later:

  • Site access and slope. Tight access and steep clay blocks take more prep.
  • Materials. Natural stone costs more than concrete pavers, and so on.
  • Drainage and soil. Reactive clay sometimes needs extra ag-lines or conditioning.
  • Size and finish level. A courtyard is not a full estate backyard.
  • Council approval. Some builds need a DA, which we can factor in.

Our promise: the price we quote is the price you pay. No call-out fee to come and look. Get your fixed-price quote.

props.label: Faq
props.html:
FAQs

Campbelltown landscaping FAQs

The things Macarthur homeowners ask us most, answered straight.

How much does landscaping cost in the Macarthur region?
It depends on the job, but our pricing guide above gives real starting ranges by project type, from a garden refresh to a full backyard makeover. Every quote is free, fixed and has no call-out fee. Tell us your block and we will price it exactly.
What is the difference between hard and soft landscaping?
Hard landscaping is the built structure: paving, retaining walls, driveways and edging. Soft landscaping is the living side: turf, garden beds, plants and mulch. Most yards need both, planned together, so levels and drainage suit the planting. We do both in-house.
Should I hire a landscape designer or a landscaping contractor?
If you only want drawings, a designer is fine. If you want the yard actually built and planted, you need a contractor too. We are both, so your design gets built by the same team, with no gap where things get lost between trades.
Is my block suitable for a retaining wall on clay soil?
Almost always, but the build has to suit reactive Wianamatta clay. That means engineered footings and proper ag-drainage behind the wall so moisture movement does not push it out. We assess the slope and soil on site and quote a wall that will hold.
Which landscaping suits a bushfire-prone block?
On bush-fringe blocks near Dharawal or the Georges River, we plan defendable space: low-flammability planting away from the house, non-combustible hardscaping close in, and clear separation from bushland. We work to the intent of Planning for Bush Fire Protection. Check your BAL rating with the RFS and council.
Do I need council approval for landscaping?
Many jobs like turf, garden beds and paving need no approval. Bigger retaining walls, structures near boundaries, or tree removal can need a development application or a permit. We flag anything that does before we start and can prepare council-ready plans. Confirm specifics with Campbelltown Council.
Do you build new-estate gardens from bare dirt?
Yes, that is a big part of what we do across the growth corridor in Bardia, Denham Court, Glenfield and Gilead. We do turnkey front and back packages that meet estate design guidelines and landscaping bond conditions, so you clear the requirement and get a finished yard.
Are you licensed and insured?
Yes, we are a licensed contractor, licence number 353-827-C. We are happy to show our credentials before any work starts, so you know exactly who is on your property.
How long does a landscaping project take?
A garden refresh can be a day or two. Paving or a retaining wall usually runs three to seven days. A full backyard makeover is often two to four weeks depending on size, access and weather. We give you a clear timeline with your fixed quote.
What is the best time of year to landscape in NSW?
Autumn and spring are ideal, with mild temperatures that help turf and plants establish before summer heat or winter frost. That said, we landscape year round here, and hard landscaping like paving and walls can be built in any season.
Do you offer same day service?
Often, yes, especially for smaller jobs, quotes and urgent tidy-ups. We are open till late, 7 days, 7am to 7pm, so call 0457 897 659 and we will tell you honestly what we can do today.
Do you charge a call-out fee?
No. Coming out to look at your job and quote it is free, every time. You only pay once you accept a fixed-price quote and we get to work. We will also beat any written quote you already have, conditions apply.
Do you service suburbs outside the immediate area?
We cover the whole Macarthur region, from the established suburbs through the family and ridge areas to the growth estates and bush-fringe blocks. If you are just outside and not sure, call and ask. We will give you a straight answer.
What other suburbs do you cover?
All 34 across the region: Airds, Ambarvale, Bardia, Blair Athol, Blairmount, Bow Bowing, Bradbury, Campbelltown, Claymore, Denham Court, Eagle Vale, Englorie Park, Eschol Park, Gilead, Glen Alpine, Glenfield, Ingleburn, Kearns, Kentlyn, Leumeah, Long Point, Macquarie Fields, Macquarie Links, Menangle Park, Minto, Minto Heights, Raby, Rosemeadow, Ruse, St Andrews, St Helens Park, Varroville, Wedderburn and Woodbine.
